steps.message: The patch has been submitted. I have modified `fastapi/routing.py` to ensure that route functions with an explicit `-> None` return type annotation automatically return a `204 No Content` status code when no other status code is specified. This was achieved by moving the `return_annotation` retrieval and adding a check using `inspect.signature` to verify the presence of a return annotation when `get_typed_return_annotation` returns `None`.

The issue was that FastAPI route functions with an explicit `-> None` return type annotation would return a `200 OK` response with a `"null"` body instead of the more appropriate `204 No Content` response. To resolve this, I modified `fastapi/routing.py` in the `APIRoute.__init__` method. I moved the call to `get_typed_return_annotation(endpoint)` so that the resulting `return_annotation` is available when determining the `status_code`. I then added logic to check if the `status_code` is `None` and the `return_annotation` is `None`. If both are true, I use `inspect.signature(endpoint).return_annotation` to determine if an explicit return annotation was provided. If it was (meaning it was explicitly `-> None`), the `status_code` is set to `204`. This ensures that `def foo() -> None:` triggers a `204` response, while `def foo():` (no annotation) continues to return `200 OK`.
